# The heart: structure and cardiac cycle

#cardio #exam-topic

## Key points
- The heart has **four chambers**: two atria receive blood, two ventricles pump it out[^1]
- Cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume, about 5 L/min at rest
- The left ventricle has the thickest wall: it must push blood around the whole body

> [!tip] Remember
> Blood always flows in one direction thanks to the four valves: tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, aortic.

## The cardiac cycle
| Phase | What happens | Valves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Diastole | Ventricles fill | AV open, semilunar closed |
| Systole | Ventricles contract | AV closed, semilunar open |

Figure: The pressure–volume loop of the left ventricle {#fig-1}

Word :: Preload: the stretch of the ventricle wall just before it contracts

## To review
- [x] Read chapter 4

# Blood pressure and its regulation

#cardio

## Short-term control
- **Baroreceptors** in the aortic arch and carotid sinus detect stretch
- Low pressure → heart rate and vessel tone go up (sympathetic)
- High pressure → heart rate goes down (vagus nerve)

> [!question] Exam question
> Why does standing up quickly sometimes make us dizzy?

Answer: blood pools in the legs, pressure drops for a second, and the baroreflex needs a few heartbeats to respond.

## Long-term control
1. The kidneys adjust blood volume
2. The renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system raises pressure when it is low
3. Hormones: ADH keeps water, ANP lets it go

Word :: Mean arterial pressure: diastolic + one third of the pulse pressure

- [ ] Redo the MAP calculations from the exercise sheet

# Respiration and gas exchange

#respiration

## Mechanics
- Inspiration: the diaphragm contracts and flattens, the lungs expand
- Expiration at rest is passive (elastic recoil)
- Compliance tells how easily the lungs stretch

## Gas exchange
Oxygen and carbon dioxide cross the **alveolar membrane** by simple diffusion. The driving force is the difference in partial pressure[^1].

| Gas | Alveolus (mmHg) | Blood (mmHg) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| O2 | 104 | 40 |
| CO2 | 40 | 45 |

> [!important] Careful
> Haemoglobin is almost saturated at 60 mmHg: that is why altitude is tolerated until about 3000 m.

[^1]: Fick's law: the rate depends on area, difference in pressure and membrane thickness.

# The kidney and the nephron

#renal

- Each kidney holds about a million nephrons
- Three steps: **filtration**, reabsorption, secretion
- The glomerular filtration rate is about 125 mL/min

## Where does what happen?
- Proximal tubule: reabsorbs about 65 % of water and all the glucose
- Loop of Henle: builds the concentration gradient
- Collecting duct: ADH decides how much water is kept

# Quiz: Financial Accounting

**1. A company buys a laptop on credit for 2 000. What changes?**

- A. Assets and liabilities both +2 000
- B. Assets +2 000, equity +2 000
- C. Only equity changes
- D. Nothing

> [!tip]- Answer
> A. Assets and liabilities both +2 000

**2. Which method sells the oldest items first?**

- A. LIFO
- B. FIFO
- C. Weighted average
- D. Specific cost

> B. FIFO

- A. 600
- B. 300
- C. 200
- D. 100

> C. 200

**4. A current ratio of 0.8 means...**

- A. comfortable liquidity
- B. possible short-term trouble
- C. high profit
- D. no debt

> [!tip]- Answer
> B. possible short-term trouble

**5. Which statement lists assets and liabilities?**

- A. Income statement
- B. Cash flow statement
- C. Balance sheet
- D. Equity statement

> [!tip]- Answer
> C. Balance sheet

> B. the cost of an asset over its life

# Course summary: Human Physiology

## 2026-10-05 1015 - Human Physiology

# The heart: structure and cardiac cycle

#cardio #exam-topic

## Key points
- The heart has **four chambers**: two atria receive blood, two ventricles pump it out[^1]
- Cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume, about 5 L/min at rest
- The left ventricle has the thickest wall: it must push blood around the whole body

> [!tip] Remember
> Blood always flows in one direction thanks to the four valves: tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, aortic.

## The cardiac cycle
| Phase | What happens | Valves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Diastole | Ventricles fill | AV open, semilunar closed |
| Systole | Ventricles contract | AV closed, semilunar open |

Figure: The pressure–volume loop of the left ventricle {#fig-1}

Word :: Preload: the stretch of the ventricle wall just before it contracts

## To review
- [x] Read chapter 4
- [ ] Draw the pressure–volume loop, see [@fig-1]
- [ ] Compare with [[Anatomy]] (heart dissection)

[^1]: Two atria, two ventricles. The right side is the lung circuit, the left side the body circuit.


## 2026-10-08 0815 - Human Physiology

# Blood pressure and its regulation

#cardio

## Short-term control
- **Baroreceptors** in the aortic arch and carotid sinus detect stretch
- Low pressure → heart rate and vessel tone go up (sympathetic)
- High pressure → heart rate goes down (vagus nerve)

> [!question] Exam question
> Why does standing up quickly sometimes make us dizzy?

Answer: blood pools in the legs, pressure drops for a second, and the baroreflex needs a few heartbeats to respond.

## Long-term control
1. The kidneys adjust blood volume
2. The renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system raises pressure when it is low
3. Hormones: ADH keeps water, ANP lets it go

Word :: Mean arterial pressure: diastolic + one third of the pulse pressure

- [ ] Redo the MAP calculations from the exercise sheet


## 2026-10-12 1015 - Human Physiology

# Respiration and gas exchange

#respiration

## Mechanics
- Inspiration: the diaphragm contracts and flattens, the lungs expand
- Expiration at rest is passive (elastic recoil)
- Compliance tells how easily the lungs stretch

## Gas exchange
Oxygen and carbon dioxide cross the **alveolar membrane** by simple diffusion. The driving force is the difference in partial pressure[^1].

| Gas | Alveolus (mmHg) | Blood (mmHg) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| O2 | 104 | 40 |
| CO2 | 40 | 45 |

> [!important] Careful
> Haemoglobin is almost saturated at 60 mmHg: that is why altitude is tolerated until about 3000 m.

[^1]: Fick's law: the rate depends on area, difference in pressure and membrane thickness.


## Synthesis

The main ideas of the course, in one page.

# Flashcards: Assets, liabilities and equity

#flashcards

**1. What is the accounting equation?**

> [!tip]- Answer
> Assets = Liabilities + Equity

**2. What does a balance sheet show?**

> [!tip]- Answer
> What a company owns and owes at one date

**3. What is an accrual?**

> [!tip]- Answer
> Income or expense counted in the period it relates to, whatever the payment date

**4. How is straight-line depreciation calculated?**

> [!tip]- Answer
> (Cost - residual value) / useful life

**5. What does FIFO mean?**

> [!tip]- Answer
> First in, first out: the oldest items are sold first

**6. What is the current ratio?**

> [!tip]- Answer
> Current assets / current liabilities

# Summary: Assets, liabilities and equity

Every transaction keeps the accounting equation in balance: assets equal liabilities plus equity.

- Assets: what the company owns
- Liabilities: what it owes
- Equity: what is left for the owners
